text:
Quinn Hughes picked up his 500th career point in Vancouver, and he did it in a Minnesota sweater. The Canucks drafted him seventh overall in 2018 out of Michigan, and on Sunday at Rogers Arena he assisted on Kirill Kaprizov's goal and scored one of his own on the power play. VAN, meanwhile, is winless in ten (0-9-1) after falling 4-2.

The final undersells how one-sided the play was. Our expected goals, a measure of the quality of chances, had MIN at 6.11 to VAN's 1.91, and our simulation of every shot says MIN deserved to win 94 percent of the time. The second period decided it: MIN out-chanced VAN 3.17 to 0.59 and scored twice, Bobby Brink on a backhand and Hughes on the power play. Maxim Shabanov opened the scoring on the man advantage late in the first, and MIN finished 2 for 5 with the extra man while VAN went 0 for 1. Leevi Meriläinen kept it from getting worse, saving about 1.6 goals more than his shots deserved.

Kaprizov made it 4-0 early in the third, and VAN's goals from Max Sasson and Brock Boeser came after the game was largely settled. Sasson, never drafted, reached the NHL as a free agent after a season in the AHL with Abbotsford, and he was named third star. For VAN, the winless run reaches ten games. MIN leaves with a convincing win and a milestone for the defenseman who now wears its colors.
